title: Composite widgets accessibility audit: density-aware focus outlines, keyboard guidance, and VPAT pack for nested headers & sparklines
creator: Ava Campbell
description: Scope: Run a targeted accessibility audit and remediation pass for a set of composite components that have regressed or lack clear guidance in the design system: nested table headers (multi-row/column headers), compact multi-select chips, row-action toolbars, and inline sparklines/small charts. Deliverables: (1) component-level remediation proposals (visual tokens + interaction patterns), (2) updated component specs in the Design System with keyboard interaction matrices, (3) VPAT evidence snippets (annotations + test cases) for each component, and (4) a lightweight QA checklist for Design & Eng to verify behavior across browsers and assistive tech. Goals: ensure focus visibility across density variants, guarantee predictable keyboard traversal for nested headers and combobox-like chips, provide fallbacks for non-visual affordances, and produce VPAT-ready evidence for product compliance reviews.
comments: 2025-02-10 — Ava: Kickoff notes: product reported two customer issues where keyboard focus disappeared when navigating nested table headers. Decided to scope a narrow remediation for composite widgets first instead of a systemwide token change.

2025-02-12 — Marco: Audit pass 1 complete for nested headers and row action toolbars. Findings: (a) focus outline is removed in compact density due to legacy token mixin; (b) header cells rely on hover-only reveal for sort controls which is not keyboard discoverable; (c) sparklines use color-only encoding for trends with insufficient contrast on dark themes.

2025-02-14 — Design review: Proposed solution — introduce a density-aware focus token (focus-contrast-level) that scales outline thickness and accessible color ramp, and add explicit keyboard affordance styles for header sort buttons (visible on focus). Consensus to avoid large token renames; create alias tokens to minimize downstream churn.

2025-02-16 — Eng feedback (PR #4129): Engineering suggests small change to the header button markup to add aria-describedby that points to a visually-hidden label describing sort state. Also flagged a performance risk for sparklines when adding DOM nodes per point; agreed to use SVG semantics and <title> elements for screen reader labels instead.

2025-02-18 — QA: Ran VoiceOver and NVDA smoke tests on macOS and Windows for nested headers. Results: focus order stable after markup change, but VoiceOver still reads both header and sort button labels twice in some cases. Action: refine accessible name calculation (avoid duplicate title attributes on ancestors).

2025-02-20 — VPAT preparation: Assembling component-level evidence. For each component we will provide: test case steps, AT reproduction notes, targeted contrast measurements, and design tokens changed. Draft evidence for 'Nested table headers' attached: drive.link/DS-NestedHeaders-vpat-draft (placeholder), needs legal review before submission.

2025-02-22 — Marco: Implemented alias token focus-contrast-level and applied to buttons, chips, and header controls. Pushed changes to the design tokens branch; awaiting token release coordination with tokens@engineering. PR: github.com/redwood-inference/design-system/pull/4211

2025-02-24 — Design QA: Verified compact chips now show a 2px focus outline with 3:1 contrast against background in high-density mode. Edge case: when chips are arranged in a focus trap (modal filter), keyboard navigation must still expose tabbable items; added acceptance criteria to checklist.

2025-02-25 — Next steps: Finalize VPAT snippets and handover to Compliance for review; schedule a small rollout with canary flag for Dedicated customers to validate behavior under our telemetry-enabled builds.
